input: An amine absorption unit has been tested at pilot scale on gas from a cement kiln, and this passage reports the principal results of that testing programme in some detail. Over a period of 45 days, operating at a rate of 11 t of carbon dioxide per day, the unit captured 89% of the carbon dioxide in the treated gas, which represents a strong level of capture performance sustained over the duration of the trial. In terms of the associated resource requirements, the steam demand was found to be 3.8 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, while the solvent loss was 2.2 kg per tonne captured, and both of these quantities are important considerations when the overall performance of the process is being assessed. It should be noted, however, that the testing extended over 45 days in total, and beyond 45 days the effect of kiln dust on the solvent remains untested, which is a significant caveat that should be borne in mind when these results are interpreted. Taken together, the results show that the unit achieved a capture level of 89% over the 45 days of testing at 11 t of carbon dioxide per day, with a steam demand of 3.8 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured and a solvent loss of 2.2 kg per tonne captured, although the longer-term behaviour of the solvent when exposed to kiln dust has yet to be established. For ease of reference, the headline figures can be restated as follows: a capture level of 89% maintained over 45 days, a steam demand of 3.8 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, and a solvent loss of 2.2 kg per tonne captured, with a further 45 days of operation needed before any longer-term trend in performance could be identified.
target: An amine absorption unit tested at pilot scale on gas from a cement kiln captured 89% of the carbon dioxide in the treated gas. The test ran over 45 days at 11 t of carbon dioxide per day. Steam demand was 3.8 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, and solvent loss was 2.2 kg per tonne captured. The figures form one result with one boundary: each was measured over the same 45 days, and the boundary of the result is the length of the test. Beyond 45 days, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent is untested. The solvent loss of 2.2 kg per tonne captured is therefore a figure for solvent that has seen 45 days of kiln gas, and it carries no information about loss rates once kiln dust has accumulated in the solvent over a longer campaign. The capture figure has the same limit in the other direction: 89% was the capture held across the test as run, and a solvent changed by kiln dust may not hold it. Steam demand, at 3.8 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, is the one figure with no stated dependence on solvent condition, and it too was measured only within the 45 days. At its tested scope, the result is a pilot unit capturing 89% of the carbon dioxide in cement-kiln gas at 11 t of carbon dioxide per day, with a steam demand of 3.8 gigajoules per tonne captured and a solvent loss of 2.2 kg per tonne captured; performance beyond 45 days, where kiln dust acts on the solvent, is unmeasured.
